1. (Currently amended) A method for restoring efficiency of a photovoltaic cell, the method comprising: illuminating a photovoltaic cell such that the photovoltaic cell receives a time integrated irradiance of __at least 5 hours equivalent to standard solar illumination__; and annealing the photovoltaic cell at a temperature above 90 degrees Celsius for a minimum of 10 minutes, the annealing performed in response to illuminating the photovoltaic cell.

2. (Currently amended) The method of Claim 1, wherein the photovoltaic cell comprises a semiconductor wafer, and wherein __the illuminating step comprises one of the following: the photovoltaic cell receives a time integrated irradiance of at least 20 hours equivalent to standard solar illumination; the photovoltaic cell receives a time integrated irradiance of at least 16 hours equivalent to standard solar illumination while the photovoltaic cell is being heated to at least 50 degrees Celsius during the illuminating step; or the photovoltaic cell is irradiated in sunlight using a solar concentrator for at least 10 hours, and the solar concentrator increases the irradiance of solar illumination on the photovoltaic cell by a factor of 2 to 5__.

3. (Currently amended) The method of Claim 2, wherein the photovoltaic cell is annealed at a temperature above 130 degrees Celsius, and wherein __the annealing step further comprises illuminating the photovoltaic cell simultaneously with the heating__.

4. (Currently amended) The method of Claim 3, wherein __the simultaneous illuminating and annealing of the photovoltaic cell is performed such that the photovoltaic cell receives a time integrated irradiance of at least 10 minutes equivalent to standard solar illumination__.

5. (Original) The method of Claim 1, wherein the semiconductor wafer is a silicon semiconductor wafer.

6. (Original) The method of Claim 1, wherein the photovoltaic cell is annealed at a temperature between 140 degrees Celsius and 210 degrees Celsius for a minimum of 2 hours.

7. (Original) The method of Claim 6, wherein the photovoltaic cell is a thin film photovoltaic cell.

8. (Original) The method of Claim 6, wherein the photovoltaic cell is an amorphous silicon thin film photovoltaic cell.

9. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the photovoltaic cell is illuminated after manufacturing of the photovoltaic cell is complete such that the photovoltaic cell produces electricity when illuminated.

10. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the photovoltaic cell is illuminated with a light source that simulates light from the sun.
